candidate.answerReason: Seven times 14 is 98, while seven times 15 is 105, so 14 is the largest permitted whole number.

methods.label: Compare consecutive multiples
methods.explanation:
We need the last whole number whose multiple of 7 is below 100. Since
\[
7\cdot14=98<100,
\qquad 7\cdot15=105>100,
\]
14 works and 15 does not. Every larger whole number has an even larger multiple of 7. Thus the largest possible number is \(\boxed{14}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: Consecutive integer products settle the strict upper bound using elementary arithmetic.
